Regression to the mean is not what you think it is. Let's say you flip a fair coin 10 times and it comes up all heads. As you flip it more and more the results are going to regress to the mean of 50% heads instead of 100%. That's not because you 'catch up' but because the actual result of the coin is 50% and as you increase the sample size it will approach that even if it stays 10 heads ahead for the rest of eternity. Eg if after 100 flips it's 60/50 then we have 54.5% heads. After 1000 flips it's 510/500 or 50.5%. After 10000 flips it's 50.05% and so on.

Applying this to the topic, a genetically linked trait does not actually regress to the mean unless its occurrence was a 'freak of nature' and not a consequence of a casual factor like genetics. Eg - the coin only goes to 50% if it's 'true' value actually is 50%! I just looked up the tallest basketball player to get a healthy sample of extreme height, increasing chances of procreation.
